deviations.claim_in_article: “Meta had run a test that caused exactly this surprise.”
deviations.issue: The article says the test actually caused someone to experience this surprise. The Ledger supports calls handled by human contract workers and a lack of appropriate disclosure, but does not report that a caller was surprised or that this reaction occurred. The source framed the test as evoking this scenario; the English wording makes the reaction sound actual.
deviations.explanation: The claim adds an unverified reaction, so changed_fact and unsupported_new_claim are true. The surrounding framing is dramatic and does not substantially change the central fact that some Muse calls were handled by people, so this is MINOR.
deviations.qualifier_text: “A call seemed to come from an AI agent.”; “In some calls through Muse, trained contract workers made the calls, not AI.”
same_fact_id_locations: We Thought It Was AI—But There Was a Person Inside Meta’s Muse
A call seemed to come from an AI agent.
But as the conversation went on, the voice was not AI at all. It was a person.
It was like someone took off an AI costume. Then a person stepped out.
